one_line_contribution: A bank-swap protocol that quantifies, in item-paired accuracy points against a measured null-replicate floor, how much of a reflective prompt optimizer's gain is bound to the particular experience bank present during optimization, plus a pre-registered head-to-head of five candidate fixes whose load-bearing question (P8) is whether that fragility is curable at deployment by lowering injection top-k or requires randomizing the optimization-time memory context.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, neither adequately dispatched. (1) Mechanism and framing: the proposal itself concedes FiD-style stochastic document dropping and randomized retrieved-context masking in RAG training curricula as the mechanistic prior, and MIPROv2/GEPA already select a final candidate against a fixed validation context, so 'the optimizer overfits the context it was tuned on' is the standard validation-overfitting story from the DSPy/MIPROv2 line rather than a new phenomenon; the only new element is that the context is a self-edited bank instead of a bootstrapped demo set, and the proposal never argues why that distinction changes the mechanism. (2) The demonstration-sensitivity literature (Min et al., 'Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations', and its successors) already establishes that quantity/format of in-context exemplars, not their content, drives most of the effect. That is exactly the pilot's 'injection volume, not content, was the causal lever' finding, and it is precisely what the neutral-block arm (P6) and the top-k arm (P8) are set up to re-derive. If either lands, the paper collapses into a known generic result about context volume, and the proposal's own pre-registration says it would then retitle. ExpeL/AWM/SSO are correctly characterized as non-threatening, since none evaluates an optimized instruction under bank turnover; they are not the danger.
strongest_objection: The primary diagnostic is degenerate and the one non-degenerate contrast is underpowered at its true unit of analysis. D_swap = acc(own) - acc(swapped) is minimized to zero by any instruction that simply ignores the memory block, so P1's 'D_swap <= 1.5 at p=1' is a manipulation check, not a prediction: memory-free optimization cannot co-adapt by construction. The only claim that distinguishes 'robustness' from 'learned to ignore memory' is P2's 'p=0.5 beats p=1 by >= 2 points under B_swap' — and that contrast is 4 optimizer seeds vs 4 optimizer seeds. Item-pairing over 800 questions does nothing for seed-level variance, which the proposal itself puts at 1-2 points; a two-sample comparison at n=4/arm with SD=1.5 has an MDE near 3-4 points, worse than the 2-point threshold P2 asks it to resolve, and worse still after the Bonferroni split to alpha=0.025 and the conjunctive rule (pooled CI excludes zero AND all 4 seeds agree in sign AND effect > 2x a between-seed SD estimated from 4 points). The modal outcome is therefore a bounded null on the paper's decisive contrast, on one task with one 7B model. Two secondary defects compound this: (a) the Stage-1 gate selects on the point estimate of D_swap at p=0 being >= 3 points and then folds the gate seed into the pooled analysis, so the headline co-adaptation number is conditioned on having passed a threshold on itself — disclosure does not remove the upward bias; (b) the P8 comparison is asymmetric, taking the best k in {1,2} for p=0 (selected on the same 800 evaluation items, so optimistically biased) against p=0.5 at a fixed k=4 with only a 2-seed spot check at k=2, which means a 'refutation' of P8 could be produced by test-set selection on the competitor alone. Separately, the stated setup 'HotpotQA distractor setting, fullwiki-style tool calls' is internally inconsistent — gold-plus-distractor paragraphs supplied in context is a different task from retrieval tool calls — and HotpotQA contamination in Qwen2.5-7B is a live confound for a study whose banks are distilled from the same dataset.
what_would_fix_it: Five concrete changes, roughly in order of importance. (1) Re-cast the primary endpoint so the degenerate solution cannot win: report memory-conditional gain under turnover, acc(instr, B_B) - acc(instr, no bank), as a co-primary alongside acc under B_swap, and pre-register that a condition with D_swap ~ 0 but zero memory-conditional gain is scored as 'learned to ignore memory', not as robustness. E3 already computes the right quantity (C) but is explicitly non-gating; promote it. (2) Reallocate the envelope from items to seeds: 800 paired items already give a within-seed MDE of 2.5 points, well past the binding constraint, so drop to n=400 items and buy 8-10 optimizer seeds at p=0 and p=0.5. Cutting E5 (8 cells) and E4 entirely funds this; both are explicitly exploratory and neither gates a claim. (3) Move the Stage-1 gate onto a dedicated seed and a dedicated split, and exclude the gate seed from the pooled primary estimate. (4) Make P8 symmetric: tune k per condition over a nested selection split disjoint from the 800 test items, report best-k-for-each rather than best-k-for-the-baseline-only against fixed-k-for-ours. (5) Run and log the dated preprint search now rather than promising it before submission, and add the query terms the current list misses ('prompt optimizer validation overfitting', 'in-context demonstration distribution shift robustness', 'agent memory non-stationarity evaluation', 'DSPy retrieval drift'). Also resolve the HotpotQA distractor-vs-tool-call contradiction and add a contamination check, or move to a task with less exposure.
missing_baseline: Cross-bank candidate selection. GEPA-style search already produces a pool of candidate instructions and picks one by validation score against the optimization-time bank; the cheapest and most obvious practitioner fix is to keep memory injection on during optimization but select or early-stop the final candidate on a held-out second bank (or on the average over two banks). It costs zero additional rollouts, it is strictly easier to deploy than either memory dropout or shard randomization, and it plausibly captures most of the robustness gain — which would leave the proposal's intervention with no cost advantage over the trivial alternative. Its absence is conspicuous given that the far more expensive 'full re-optimization on every bank change' is included as the upper bound. A second, related omission: joint optimization against both B_A and B_B (multi-bank domain randomization) as the true robustness ceiling, which would bracket shard randomization from above and tell the reader whether p=0.5's gap to the ceiling is 1 point or 6.
preprint_collision: The check reports that every web-search call failed and that the author has zero verified evidence about recent preprints. By the standard that applies here, that is not a neutral: novelty on both the framing (optimizer-memory co-adaptation as train/deploy context-distribution mismatch) and the diagnostic (bank-swap evaluation of an optimized instruction) is simply unestablished, and this is the second consecutive draft in which the search failed, which reads less like bad luck than like a step that keeps being deferred. The author's mitigation — restructuring the contribution as a comparative fix table so a priority collision is survivable — is the right instinct and is why this is not an automatic reject, but it does not let a reviewer conclude the work is new. I am not able to name a specific colliding arXiv preprint (no search available to me either), so I score this as an unverified novelty claim rather than a demonstrated collision. Two further problems with the check as written: the promised query list omits the terms most likely to surface a collision from the prompt-optimization side rather than the memory side ('prompt optimizer overfits validation context', 'instruction search generalization retrieval shift', 'DSPy/GEPA candidate selection robustness'), and the stated fallback ('if a preprint already performs a bank-swap evaluation, the contribution reduces to the fix table plus P8') understates the damage, since P8's most likely outcome per the proposal's own risk section is that deployment-time top-k tuning wins, leaving a fix table whose headline row is a negative result on the authors' own method.
